title: CPI for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW), General Index
description: All-India general index of the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (base 2016=100), compiled monthly by the Labour Bureau from retail prices in 317 markets across 88 industrial centres, released on the last working day of the following month. It determines dearness allowance for central government employees and wage indexation, so it is watched for fiscal and wage-bargaining effects. History here starts in September 2020, when the 2016-base series took effect; the older 2001-base series is not spliced on. A few months (August 2023, December 2023, January 2025) are missing because the Labour Bureau table omits the all-India row for them; they are left blank, not estimated. Year-on-year inflation is computed from the index.
source: Labour Bureau, Ministry of Labour & Employment

qna.question: What is CPI-IW?
qna.answer: A fixed-basket retail price index for households of industrial workers (factory, mining, plantation, railway, port and electricity workers), covering food, pan/tobacco, clothing, housing, fuel and light and miscellaneous items. The Labour Bureau publishes the All-India index and 88 centre indices.^Its main practical use is to set the dearness allowance of central government staff and pensioners.

qna.question: How does it differ from the national CPI?
qna.answer: CPI-IW has a different basket (weighted to industrial workers' consumption), covers 88 industrial centres rather than all districts, and has base 2016=100, so its inflation can differ materially from MoSPI's CPI (it has a heavier food weight and no rural component). It is not a replacement for headline CPI.

qna.question: Caveats?
qna.answer: Values for the latest month can be revised in the next release. The series on this page starts in September 2020 because the 2016 base took effect then. Year-on-year rates are computed from rounded one-decimal index values and may differ from the Labour Bureau's published rates by a few basis points.
